_doc: STAGING. General pack, and the one the bench LIKED rather than tolerated. Wing 7's finding is the brief: across 59 clues no woman had a role outside the kitchen or the receiving end of a joke. Laundry Day is the fix — the quiet, repeated, unwatched domestic hour, written with interiority. So the person in these clues is thinking, deciding, and keeping count, never being observed doing a chore. No clue here is a joke at anyone's expense. Standard general gate still binds: position, time or habit, never a category.

theme.name: Laundry Day
theme.blurb: The quiet hour nobody watches, repeated every week for a lifetime.

boards._note: Letter-set on loan from barbershop, which keeps 15 of its 16 spare boards.
boards.scene: Sorting, which is where the decisions get made

clues.paints: On the knee of the good trousers, and today is when that gets decided
clues.pant: Checked at both pockets before anything goes in, having learned once
clues.pin: Found at the bottom of the drum, and where it came from is a mystery
clues.spin: Chosen lower than the label says, because the label does not know this machine
clues.stain: Worked at with a thumbnail under the tap for longer than it is worth
clues.snap: The waistband, tested, and the answer decides whether it goes in or out

boards.scene: The first load, and the smell of it

clues.pianos: Practice upstairs, the same eight bars, all the way through the first load
clues.pin: Straightened and put on the sill, because it will be needed
clues.soap: Measured properly by one person in the house and by eye by everyone else
clues.spin: The noise it makes at the top of the cycle, which is how you know the load is uneven
clues.pain: In the lower back, from the third bend at the machine door
clues.pains: Taken over one shirt, on a day when nothing else got that much attention

boards.scene: Ironing, at the board by the window

clues.senior: Taught you to do collars first, and was right, and you have never said so
clues.iron: Filled with the wrong water for years before anybody mentioned it
clues.noise: From the street, at the level where it stops registering as anything
clues.rinse: Given to the one thing that came out smelling of the machine
clues.risen: The steam, into a face turned deliberately away from it
clues.sire: On the paperwork in the pocket of the coat, which is why the coat is not going in

clues.actors: On the poster in the stairwell, faded, from a film nobody in the building saw
clues.cart: Loaded so it can be pushed with one hand and the door held with the other
clues.sort: Done on the way down, mentally, so the machines can be claimed faster
clues.coat: Kept on for the first ten minutes because the room has not warmed up
clues.cost: Counted in coins, in advance, and the sum has not changed in three years
clues.oats: Left on the counter upstairs, which is what you think about on the way back

boards.scene: The pile of things that need a hand, not a machine

clues.amends: The hem, badly, and it holds for two years, which counts
clues.mend: Put off from March to August and then done in eleven minutes
clues.seam: Gone at the shoulder, on the shirt that is not worth it and gets fixed anyway
clues.dame: Whose needle case this was, and whose handwriting is on the lid
clues.mean: What the thread does when it will not go through, at the third attempt
clues.made: The decision to keep it, which is the whole reason the box came down

boards.scene: The airer, and the weather forecast

clues.foiled: By rain at two, having hung the whole load out at noon
clues.fold: Done straight from the line while it is still warm, which is the best minute of it
clues.lid: Of the machine, left up on purpose so the drum can dry out
clues.field: Beyond the fence, and where your eye goes while your hands keep working
clues.idle: The ten minutes waiting on the last spin, which are nothing of the kind
clues.file: Of things to hang next, arranged in your head before you reach the door

boards.scene: What is playing while it gets done

clues.gospel: From the phone propped against the powder box, at a volume for one person
clues.lose: One sock a load, reliably, and the arithmetic has never been explained
clues.peg: Split at the spring, kept in the bag anyway, and it still works
clues.pole: Propped under the middle of the line, because the load is heavier than it looks
clues.slope: Of the line by the time it is full, and the adjustment made without thinking
clues.goes: The last thing on, and then you stand there a second before going in

boards.scene: The airing cupboard, and who knows the system

clues.intros: Of the songs, all you hear, because the phone is skipping in another room
clues.iron: Kept on the top shelf where it has to be reached for, on purpose
clues.sort: By bed, not by person, which is the system and it took years to settle
clues.riot: In there by November, when nobody else has put anything back correctly
clues.rots: What the towel at the bottom does, found in spring, and thrown out quietly
clues.trio: Of shelves, and every one of them is a different household's worth of rules

boards.scene: The last hour, and the standing up

clues.liners: In the drawers, changed once a year, and today happens to be the day
clues.line: Wiped down before anything touches it, which is the step people skip
clues.rinse: The cloth, twice, and hang it over the tap in the way it always goes
clues.rise: What you do from the chair when the machine stops, before it finishes beeping
clues.risen: The pile on the bed, higher than the day looked when it started
clues.siren: Outside, and everything in the room stops for it and then carries on

boards.scene: Towels, which are their own event

clues.lowest: Setting the dryer has, and the only one that does not wreck them
clues.lose: The good one, to somebody else's bathroom, permanently
clues.towel: Folded in three because it is the only way it fits the shelf
clues.stole: The warm one straight off the pile, and would do it again
clues.slow: The whole load, deliberately, because rushing towels is how they go hard
clues.west: Facing window, which is why the airer lives where it lives

boards.scene: Whites, and the war on the collar

clues.metals: In the water here, which is the real reason nothing stays white
clues.seam: Under the arm, checked every time, because that is where it always goes first
clues.steam: Held over the kettle, an old trick from someone, and it half works
clues.melts: The plastic button, on a setting chosen too confidently
clues.least: Favourite job in the house, and still done every single week
clues.salt: On the winter coat hem, brushed off dry, never washed in

clues.pastor: Will not notice, and that is not the point and never was
clues.soap: The good one, kept separate, used on four things a week
clues.sort: The shirts out the night before so the morning has one less argument in it
clues.roast: In the oven while this is happening, and both are being timed at once
clues.strap: On the shoe, wiped with the cloth that is already out
clues.past: Ten, and still going, and nobody in the house knows that
